description: An additive oscillator of up to 64 sine partials whose pitch, amplitude and phase are given as typed arithmetic, one expression worked out afresh for every partial

params.text: Sets the value of the variable x that the expressions can refer to; it multiplies whatever is at the jack below it, and reads straight through as its own value while that jack is empty
Sets the value of the variable y that the expressions can refer to; it multiplies whatever is at the jack below it, and reads straight through as its own value while that jack is empty
Sets the value of the variable z that the expressions can refer to; it multiplies whatever is at the jack below it, and reads straight through as its own value while that jack is empty
Sets the seed for the per-partial random numbers that the expressions read as r, 0 to 1000; a new set is drawn at every trigger
Freezes the expressions where they are: the partials keep sounding but stop being recalculated, and triggers are ignored until it is released
Sets how many partials are calculated, 1 to 64; the figure is shown beside the letter n on the display

inputs.text: Restarts the envelope and draws a new set of random numbers for the partials; it fires on a rise past 0.1V and arms again once the voltage falls back to 0.1V or below
Sets the fundamental frequency at one volt per octave, 0V giving C4
The voltage the x knob scales; with nothing patched it reads 1V, so the knob alone sets x
The voltage the y knob scales; with nothing patched it reads 1V, so the knob alone sets y
The voltage the z knob scales; with nothing patched it reads 1V, so the knob alone sets z
A voltage above 0V here freezes the expressions in the same way as the button

outputs.text: The sum of every partial, five times the total of the sines; nothing limits it, so how loud it gets rests entirely on the amplitude expression

notes: The module makes no sound until something is typed into the display and a trigger arrives
The nine lines on the display are, from top to bottom, the variables j, k and l, a time warp, the envelope attack and decay, and then the pitch, amplitude and phase of each partial
The header above the display names whichever of the nine lines the mouse is over
The nine expressions belong to one display rather than to separate controls, so no click on them reaches this help
The expressions are worked out in the order they are listed, so a line referring to one below it reads the previous partial's value rather than this partial's
This module is mono: it reads one channel from every jack and sends one channel out
menu: Quality: Low, Standard, High, Very High, Ultra — sets how often the expressions are worked out, once every 128 samples at Low and once every 2 samples at Ultra
Use Classic Theme — returns the panel to the original untinted artwork, which no entry in the Panel Theme list will give back
